subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that active skill's host run while generic exec remains isolated from unrelated skill secrets?
rationale: The bug and docs expectation are source-backed, but the repair changes the credential-to-exec boundary and must be reconciled with the adjacent skill-secret leak risk.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name check, while preserving dangerous-name rejection and stripping unrelated active skill secrets from generic exec.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare each sensitive env name in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys are not expected to work.

options.title: Redesign the secret contract
options.body: Defer this bypass and define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit keys explicitly configured for the active skill to pass the sensitive-name check, while preserving dangerous-name rejection and stripping unrelated active skill secrets from generic exec.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent merged history in the overlapping skill env and SecretRef runtime path.
